exposure: universal screening strategy protocol (including thyroid dysfunction, gestational diabetes, morphology and growth scans)
cohort: The study included healthy grand multiparous women aged >=35 years who delivered between 2011-2012 (selective screening group) or 2016-2017 (universal screening group) at Jordan University Hospital.
finding: Implementing new perinatal care protocols, including universal screening, significantly decreased the rate of cesarean section in grand multiparous women with advanced maternal age, but did not affect other pregnancy or neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Implementing universal screening significantly reduced the cesarean section rate from 45% in the selective screening group to 1% in the universal screening group.
